title: Compatibility of the exact-couple differential
statement:
Let $\square$ be a cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ have torsion cohomology with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$, and let $A_q=g^{-1}Rf_*\tau_{\leq q}K$, $G_q=g^{-1}Rf_*\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$, $B_q=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K$, $H_q=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$, the two exchanged truncation triangles $A_{q-1}\xrightarrow{i_q}A_q\xrightarrow{j_q}G_q\xrightarrow{k_q}A_{q-1}[1]$, $B_{q-1}\xrightarrow{i'_q}B_q\xrightarrow{j'_q}H_q\xrightarrow{k'_q}B_{q-1}[1]$ and the exchange maps $e_q=\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q}K}$, $\bar e_q=\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]}$ between them be as in [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples] [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Use the standard cohomological shift convention $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$, so that $\mathcal H^{n}(M[1])=\mathcal H^{n+1}(M)$, and let the connecting maps $k_q$, $k'_q$ be the images of the connecting map of $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to$ followed by the shift-commutation isomorphisms of $g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ (the identity for the inverse images [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]; for $Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] the comparison of the K-injective resolutions $K[1]\to I(K[1])$ and $K[1]\to I(K)[1]$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]). Index the two couples as in [def-sp-exact-couple]: $D_A^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(A_q)$, $E_A^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(G_q)$, $\alpha=\mathcal H(i_{q+1})$, $g=\mathcal H(j_q)$, $f=\mathcal H(k_q)$, and likewise $D_B,E_B$. Then:

(1) both are exact couples, and $t_D=\mathcal H^{p+q}(e_q)$, $t_E=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\bar e_q)$ form a morphism of exact couples; in particular they commute with the connecting maps: $\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(e_{q-1})\circ\mathcal H^{p+q}(k_q)=\mathcal H^{p+q}(k'_q)\circ\mathcal H^{p+q}(\bar e_q)$;

(2) the induced maps $E_{A,r}\to E_{B,r}$ ($r\geq2$) of the spectral sequences of the two couples commute with every differential $d_r$;

(3) the $E_2$ map in bidegree $(p,q)$, read through the identifications $\mathcal H^{p+q}(G_q)\cong g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)$ and $\mathcal H^{p+q}(H_q)\cong R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ given by the same shift-commutation isomorphisms and $\mathcal H^{p+q}(N[-q])=\mathcal H^p(N)$, is the degree-$p$ exchange map of the torsion sheaf $F=\mathcal H^q(K)$,

$$
 \mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,F}):\ g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\longrightarrow
 R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K).
$$

proof.text: **Step 1 (the two couples are exact).** With $v=f_*$ in [def-sp-truncation-couple], the couple $(D_A,E_A)$ is $g^{-1}$ applied termwise to the truncation couple of $K$: $\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}M)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(M)$ naturally in $M$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], the shift-commutation isomorphism of $g^{-1}$ is the identity, and $Rv$ on $\operatorname{Ch}^+$ computes $Rf_*$ as recorded in [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations]. That couple is exact [lem-sp-truncation-couple-exact], and $g^{-1}$ is an exact functor of abelian sheaves [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so it preserves the three equalities $\ker=\operatorname{im}$ of [def-sp-exact-couple]; hence $(D_A,E_A)$ is exact. With $v=f'_*$, the couple $(D_B,E_B)$ is the truncation couple of $g'^{-1}K$: $g'^{-1}$ is exact, so it commutes with canonical truncation ($\tau_{\leq q}M$ is built from $M^r$, $r<q$, and $\ker d^q_M$, and exact functors preserve kernels), $g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K=\tau_{\leq q}g'^{-1}K$, $g'^{-1}(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])=\mathcal H^q(g'^{-1}K)[-q]$, and $g'^{-1}$ carries the truncation triangle of $K$ to that of $g'^{-1}K$; $g'^{-1}K$ is bounded below with $\mathcal H^q=0$ for $q<a$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. Hence $(D_B,E_B)$ is exact by [lem-sp-truncation-couple-exact].

source.place: Lemma 0DDE (lemma-proper-base-change, line 18708), proof: the spectral sequences E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*H^q(E) and E'_2^{p,q}=R^pf'_*(g')^{-1}H^q(E) ('some details omitted'; Stacks constructs them by Cartan-Eilenberg resolutions, the blueprint by truncation couples, def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples)

proof.text: **Step 2 (the exchange maps form a morphism of the two triangles).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated] (2) to the truncation triangle $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\xrightarrow{\delta_q}\tau_{\leq q-1}K[1]$ (a triangle in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]). Its image triangles under $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $\Psi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$, with the third arrow followed by the shift-commutation isomorphism, are exactly the two rows $(A_{q-1},A_q,G_q,i_q,j_q,k_q)$ and $(B_{q-1},B_q,H_q,i'_q,j'_q,k'_q)$ of [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples]. Hence $e_q i_q=i'_q e_{q-1}$, $\bar e_q j_q=j'_q e_q$ and $e_{q-1}[1]\circ k_q=k'_q\circ\bar e_q$: the first two squares are the naturality of $\Ex_\square$, the third is its compatibility with the shift. This is the content of 'commutes with the connecting maps' at the level of triangles.

source.place: Lemma 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact, line 2290), for the shift isomorphism of the right adjoints; Definition of a morphism of triangles, Tag 0145 (derived.tex, section on triangulated categories)

proof.text: **Step 3 (a morphism of exact couples).** Apply the functor $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ to the three commutative squares of Step 2 (the first one for $q+1$), using $\mathcal H^{p+q}(M[1])=\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(M)$ (same cycles and boundaries, the sign of the differential being irrelevant), so that $\mathcal H^{p+q}(e_{q-1}[1])=\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(e_{q-1})$. One gets $\alpha_B\circ t_D=t_D\circ\alpha_A$ on $D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1}$, $g_B\circ t_D=t_E\circ g_A$ on $D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q}$, and $f_B\circ t_E=t_D\circ f_A$ on $E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1}$, which is the displayed identity of (1). These are the three conditions of a morphism of exact couples (Stacks, Homology, Definition 011Q (2), read bidegree by bidegree), so $(t_D,t_E)$ is a morphism of the exact couples of Step 1, compatible with the connecting maps $f_A,f_B$.

source.place: Definition 12.21.1 (definition-exact-couple, Tag 011Q), part (2): morphism of exact couples

proof.text: **Step 4 (all pages and all differentials).** By [lem-sp-couple-morphism] the morphism $(t_D,t_E)$ of exact couples induces for every $r\geq2$ a map $\varphi_r:E_{A,r}\to E_{B,r}$ of the pages of the spectral sequences of the couples ([def-sp-exact-couple]: $E_2=E$, $E_{r+1}=E'_r$), commuting with the differentials $d_r$, with $\varphi_2=t_E$. Written out for one derivation (Stacks, Homology, Lemma 011R and Definition 011S): $d_B t_E=g_Bf_Bt_E=g_Bt_Df_A=t_Eg_Af_A=t_Ed_A$, so $t_E$ maps $\ker d_A$ into $\ker d_B$ and $\operatorname{im}d_A$ into $\operatorname{im}d_B$ and induces $E'_A\to E'_B$; $t_D\alpha_A=\alpha_Bt_D$ gives $t_D(\operatorname{im}\alpha_A)\subseteq\operatorname{im}\alpha_B$, i.e. $D'_A\to D'_B$; these commute with $\alpha'$ (restriction of $\alpha$), with $f'$ (induced by $f$) and with $g'$ (if $y=\alpha_A(y')$ then $t_Dy=\alpha_B(t_Dy')$ and $g'_B(t_Dy)=\overline{g_B(t_Dy')}=\overline{t_E g_A(y')}$). So the derived morphism is again a morphism of exact couples, and induction on $r$ gives the compatibility with $d_{r}=g^{(r-2)}\circ f^{(r-2)}$ and with the connecting maps $f^{(r-2)}$ of every derived couple. This is (2).

source.place: Lemma 12.21.2 (lemma-derived-exact-couple, Tag 011R) and Definition 12.21.3 (Tag 011S); functoriality in the couple is not stated there and is written out here

proof.text: **Step 5 (the $E_2$ map).** Let $F=\mathcal H^q(K)$. By Step 4, $\varphi_2^{p,q}=t_E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,F[-q]})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated] (1) with $n=-q$, $\Ex_{\square,F[-q]}=(\zeta^{(-q)}_F)^{-1}\circ\Ex_{\square,F}[-q]\circ\xi^{(-q)}_F$, where $\xi^{(-q)}_F:G_q\xrightarrow{\sim}(g^{-1}Rf_*F)[-q]$ and $\zeta^{(-q)}_F:H_q\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F)[-q]$ are the shift-commutation isomorphisms. Applying $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ and $\mathcal H^{p+q}(N[-q])=\mathcal H^p(N)$, the map $t_E^{p,q}$ becomes $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,F}):\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}Rf_*F)\to\mathcal H^p(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F)$ under the identifications $E_A^{p,q}\cong\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}Rf_*F)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^p(Rf_*F)=g^{-1}R^pf_*F$ ([lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], $R^p$ as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]) and $E_B^{p,q}\cong\mathcal H^p(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F)=R^pf'_*(g'^{-1}F)$. That is the degree-$p$ exchange map $g^{-1}R^pf_*F\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}F$ induced by $\Ex_{\square,F}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], the map whose bijectivity for torsion $F$ is [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-assembly] and is used in Step 4 of [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below]. This is (3); the identifications are the ones [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples] writes as equalities, made explicit.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 0DDE (etale-cohomology.tex line 18708, 'some details omitted', via Cartan-Eilenberg spectral sequences) and Stacks Homology 011Q-011S (exact couples, derived couple), and against the blueprint nodes def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples, lem-sp-couple-morphism, def-sp-exact-couple, def-sp-truncation-couple. The imported one-paragraph proof asserted that the exchange maps commute with the connecting maps 'by naturality'; naturality gives only two of the three squares, the third (with the connecting map k_q) needs the compatibility of Ex with the shift isomorphisms of g^{-1}Rf_* and Rf'_*g'^{-1}, which no node stated: new node lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated (unsplit). The same compatibility is needed for the E_2 identification H^{p+q}(Ex_{F[-q]}) = H^p(Ex_F). The statement was made precise (objects, indexing as in def-sp-exact-couple, shift convention, which identifications read the E_2 map), without changing its content. Proof now five steps: exactness of both couples (lem-sp-truncation-couple-exact plus exactness of g^{-1}, g'^{-1}), the morphism of triangles (new node), the morphism of exact couples (elementary), all pages and differentials (lem-sp-couple-morphism, with the derivation written out from Stacks 011R), and the E_2 map. def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples is a real dependency (it defines the objects A_q, G_q, B_q, H_q, the triangles and the maps e_q, bar e_q); what it gives as 'first graded component' names only source and target, the identification with H^p(Ex_F) is Step 5 here. lem-sp-couple-morphism (unit sk-prop-av-pqf-finite) is used as a generic tool lemma, as the blueprint cites it.
